questions.stem: With what is an Integration Hub normally, and incorrectly, confused?
options: Messaging tools such as Slack and MS Teams
Data stores such as a Data Warehouse, Data Lake or Data Lakehouse
Network firewalls
Backup and mirroring systems
Source code repositories
questions.explanation: An Integration Hub is normally confused with data stores like Data Warehouse, Data Lake and Data Lakehouse, which is not correct.

options: A central store that keeps a copy of all enterprise data
A tool for compressing data before transfer
A network device that routes traffic between offices
A single central place from which instructions are sent to internal and external systems to perform actions
A dashboard for monitoring query performance
questions.explanation: An Integration Hub is a single central place from where you can send instructions to internal and external systems to perform some actions.

questions.stem: What does an Integration Hub consist of?
options: Spokes, each of which consists of a number of steps for actions
Tables, each of which holds a set of records
Nodes, each of which stores a share of the data
Layers, each of which abstracts a data source
Mirrors, each of which replicates a database
questions.explanation: An Integration Hub consists of Spokes, and each Spoke consists of a number of steps for actions.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT among the generic steps an Integration Hub Spoke can perform?
options: Run commands on external servers
Send messages such as Rest or SOAP
Allow parsers
Send SQL commands to databases
Store the enterprise's historical data for analytics
questions.explanation: Generic steps include creating actions for external systems, running commands on external servers, sending Rest or SOAP messages, allowing parsers and sending SQL commands; storing historical data is a data store's job, not a Spoke's.

questions.stem: In the SharePoint example for Integration Hub, what is the benefit when 100 users all want to delete a file?
options: Each user is given a personal copy of SharePoint
The file is deleted once and the other 99 requests are ignored
All 100 users can reuse the same Spoke created to delete files in SharePoint instead of repeating every step
SharePoint automatically grants all users administrator rights
The deletions are queued and processed overnight
questions.explanation: Without a hub each user must go through the same steps; with an Integration Hub all 100 users can reuse the single Spoke built for deleting files in SharePoint.

questions.stem: What does a Spoke for an external system such as SharePoint contain?
options: Connections, credentials and the actions to be performed
A full backup of the external system's data
The source code of the external system
A mirror of the external system's database
The external system's licence agreement
questions.explanation: A Spoke consists of the connections, credentials and actions to be performed on the external system, such as SharePoint.

questions.stem: Why do most applications, portals and systems now allow the use of Spokes?
options: Because Spokes make their data larger and richer
Because Spokes replace the need for user accounts
Because Spokes remove all security checks
Because Spokes speed up database queries
Because Spokes assist them in limiting the actions performed in their system
questions.explanation: Applications allow Spokes because a Spoke helps them limit the actions that can be performed in their system.

questions.stem: Which reason is given for why Integration Hubs are needed?
options: Third-party systems now demand fully custom connectivity from every client
Third-party systems no longer allow custom connectivity, so pre-built Spokes are the way forward
Data warehouses can no longer store external data
Custom connectors are cheaper than pre-built Spokes
Regulators require every integration to be hand-coded
questions.explanation: Third-party systems no longer allow custom connectivity, which makes pre-built Spokes the way forward.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT listed among the generic Spokes for an Integration Hub?
options: MS Teams
Slack
Jira
Salesforce
Dropbox
questions.explanation: The listed generic Spokes include CISCO WebEx, MS Teams, Slack, Zoom, GitHub, Jira, Twitter, Dropbox, Google, SharePoint and Amazon/AWS; Salesforce is not among them.

questions.stem: What benefits do pre-built Spokes in an Integration Hub provide?
options: Unlimited data extracts from any system
Automatic data quality correction
No duplicate connections for the same data, no unknown data extracts, and data allowed only within a defined scope
Faster hardware performance for external servers
Elimination of credentials for external systems
questions.explanation: Pre-built Spokes avoid duplicated connections for the same set of data, prevent unknown data extracts and allow data only within a defined scope, as well as offering reusability and a single interface.
